# About This Script

This script shows the workflow for evaluating the relationship of Community Weighted Mean (CWM) with raw functional traits and our environmental drivers.
The pipeline executes the following steps:

1) Organize raw trait data of terrestrial ferns from the Southern Atlantic Forest (SAF).

2) Calculates CWM values for each trait frameworks.

3) Fits linear models to evaluate relationships between CWM and environmental drivers.

4) Tests model residuals for spatial structure using Moran's I and Spatial Eigenvector Maps (MEM).

5) Evaluates model robustness against sampling effort using Cook's distance correlations.

The resulting output of this script is the main content of Table 1 and Appendix S11.

# Packages 

Again, multiple packages are required to run this script, most of
them are available on CRAN, see below.

```{r}
# Clear the environment and load required packages
rm(list = ls()) ## Empty environment
gc() # Clean up memory

# Required libraries (some are commented out for optional installation)
library(car)          # Evaluate the influence of points in model's predictions  
library(conflicted)   # Manage conflicts between packages
library(tidyverse)    # Data manipulation and visualization
library(openxlsx)     # Export results to Excel
library(vegan)        # Ecological analysis (e.g., community matrix)
library(readxl)       # Read Excel files
library(reshape2)     # Alternative reshaping tools
library(SYNCSA)       # Trait-based community ecology
library(jtools)       # Model summary output formatting
library(interactions) # For interaction terms in models
library(bbmle)        # Model selection and AIC comparison
library(here)         # To establish the path context


# Reproducibility settings
set.seed(811)              # Reproducible randomization
options(scipen = 999)      # Avoid scientific notation in numeric output
conflicts_prefer(dplyr::filter(), dplyr::mutate()) # Prefer dplyr functions
```

# Community Matrix 
Again we load and adjust the community matrix. The site-by-species abundance data is reshaped into a matrix filled with absolute taxon frequencies.

```{r}
# Load species frequency data (site x species matrix)
d <- read_xlsx(here("data/data_ferns.xlsx"), sheet = "w_matrix")

# Build a community matrix of absolute frequencies
w_matrix <- reshape2::acast(
  site ~ taxa,
  data = d,
  value.var = "FA_New",
  fun.aggregate = sum
) %>%
  round(digits = 2)

head(w_matrix) 
```

# X Variables 
Now, the predictors...

```{r}
x_ncor <- read_xlsx(here("data/data_ferns.xlsx"), sheet = 'e_matrix') %>%
  dplyr::filter(Site %in% rownames(w_matrix)) |>
  column_to_rownames("Site")
```

# Trait Matrix 
Finally, the trait matrix. Here we will transform each trait to binary (presence/absence).

```{r}
#Load trait matrix
t_matrix <- read_xlsx( here("data/data_ferns.xlsx"), sheet = 't_matrix') 

# Convert categorical trait variables into binary format (presence/absence)
rhiz_type <- table(t_matrix$taxa, t_matrix$rhizome_type)
morph <- table(t_matrix$taxa, t_matrix$frond_morphology)

# Create trait matrix: species x traits (binary + numeric)
t <- cbind.data.frame(
  diam = t_matrix[order(t_matrix$taxa), ]$rhizome_diameter,
  r_comp = rhiz_type[order(rownames(rhiz_type)), "Compact"],
  r_cr = rhiz_type[order(rownames(rhiz_type)), "Short-Creeping"],
  r_lr = rhiz_type[order(rownames(rhiz_type)), "Long-Creeping"],
  lmseg = t_matrix[order(order(t_matrix$taxa)), ]$laminae_dissection,
  ltri = t_matrix[order(t_matrix$taxa), ]$laminae_pubescence,
  buds = t_matrix[order(t_matrix$taxa), ]$proliferous_buds,
  ind = t_matrix[order(t_matrix$taxa), ]$indusium,
  ldim = morph[order(rownames(morph)), 'Dimorphic'],
  chl = t_matrix[order(order(t_matrix$taxa)), ]$spore_chlorophyll
) %>%
  filter(rownames(.) %in% colnames(w_matrix))

# Inspect resulting trait matrix
dim(t)
head(t)
glimpse(t)
view(t)
```

# Organizing the Raw Dataset 

We organize the dataset using SYNCSA.

```{r}
trait_raw <- organize.syncsa(
  w_matrix,
  traits = t,
  envir = x_ncor
)
identical(rownames(trait_raw$traits), colnames(trait_raw$community))

saveRDS(file = here("data/org_data.RDS", trait_raw) )  # Save for reproducibility
```

# Compute CWM
Now we will compute the Community Weighted Mean for each trait, but using absolute frequency as weight.

```{r}
cwm_values <- matrix.t(trait_raw$community, trait_raw$traits)$matrix.T %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column('Site') %>%
  add_column(trait_raw$environmental)
```

# Model Selection
Now we will select the best model for each trait, as following:
1) Creating a list of models names (see Appendix S1 for the hypothesis of each model);
2) Elaborating the linear models, based on the list;
3) Select the most parsimonious models based on AICc;
4) Filter only the best model (dAICc = 0);
5) Save in a new object for summarize in a table.

## Rhizome diameter 

```{r}
# Create list of candidate models to explain this trait 
models <- c(
  "diam ~ max_temp, data = cwm_values",
  "diam ~ max_temp + ann_prec,data = cwm_values",
  "diam ~ ann_prec*prec_seas",
  "diam ~ nitrogen, data =cwm_values",
  "diam ~ cec, data = cwm_values",
  "diam ~ nitrogen + cec, data = cwm_values",
  "diam ~ prec_wam, data = cwm_values",
  "diam ~ 1"
)

# Fit linear models
md1 <- lm(diam ~ max_temp_wam + plot_size + samp_size, data = cwm_values)

md2 <- lm(
  diam ~ max_temp_wam + ann_prec + plot_size + samp_size,
  data = cwm_values
)

md3 <- lm(
  diam ~ ann_prec * prec_seas + plot_size + samp_size,
  data = cwm_values
)

md4 <- lm(diam ~ nitrogen + plot_size + samp_size, data = cwm_values)

md5 <- lm(diam ~ cec + plot_size + samp_size, data = cwm_values)

md6 <- lm(diam ~ nitrogen + cec + plot_size + samp_size, data = cwm_values)

md7 <- lm(diam ~ prec_warm + plot_size + samp_size, data = cwm_values)

md8 <- lm(diam ~ 1 + plot_size + samp_size, data = cwm_values)

# Select the best model 
sel_md <- AICctab(
  md1,
  md2,
  md3,
  md4,
  md5,
  md6,
  md7,
  md8,
  base = T,
  delta = T,
  mnames = models
)
class(sel_md) <- "data.frame" #insert class at ictab
sel_md

# Filter the best model
result_diam <- cbind.data.frame(
  models = rownames(sel_md),
  sel_md,
  row.names = NULL
) %>%
  filter(dAICc == 0)

mod_diam <- md3
summary(md3, digits = 3)
```

```{r}
  md3,
  md4,
  md5,
  md6,
  base = T,
  delta = T,
  mnames = models
)

class(sel_md) <- "data.frame" #insert class at ictab

sel_md

result_lmor <- cbind.data.frame(
  models = rownames(sel_md),
  sel_md,
  row.names = NULL
) %>%
  filter(., dAICc == 0)

summary(md2)

mod_ldim <- md2
```

```{r}
models <- c(

)
```

```{r}
      rep("chl", length(grep("chl", .$models)))
    ),
    .before = AICc
  )

forw

# Changing models names to predictors names only
result <- gsub("cwm_values.*~ ", "", forw$models) %>%
  gsub("x_ncor\\$", "", .) %>%
  gsub(", data.*", "", .) %>%
  mutate(dplyr::select(forw, -models), predictors = ., .before = AICc)

# Separating good from bad models

bad_mods <- result[rows, ]
```

```{r}
  file = here('outputs/cwm_raw_results.xlsx'),
  rowNames = T,
  overwrite = T
)
```

# Model Robustness and Cook's Distance Diagnostics (Table 1; Appendix S12)

Again, we will evaluate influential data points using Cook's distance and 
calculate Kendall correlation with log-transformed sample area size. 

We will use the results produced here as the Appendix S12 and in Table 1.

```{r}
cwm_values$cook_diam <- cooks.distance(mod_diam) 
cwm_values$cook_rcomp <- cooks.distance(mod_rcomp) 
cwm_values$cook_rcreep <- cooks.distance(mod_rcr) 
cwm_values$cook_rlr <- cooks.distance(mod_lr) 
cwm_values$cook_mseg <- cooks.distance(mod_lmseg) 
cwm_values$cook_ind <- cooks.distance(mod_ind) 
cwm_values$cook_dim <- cooks.distance(mod_ldim) 
cwm_values$cook_chl <- cooks.distance(mod_chl) 

# Get names of columns
cook_cols <- c("cook_diam", "cook_rcomp", "cook_rcreep", "cook_rlr", 
               "cook_mseg", "cook_ind", "cook_dim", "cook_chl")
# Create the harmonized names to export the data
names <- c("Rhiz. Diameter", "Rhiz. Compact", "Rhiz. Short-Creeping", 
           "Rhiz. Long-Creeping", "Lam. Multipinnate", "Indusium presence", 
           "Frond Dimorphism", "Spore Chlorophyll")

# Compute Kendall results 
kendall_results <- sapply(cwm_values[cook_cols], function(x) {
  test <- cor.test(x, log10(cwm_values$samp_size), method = "kendall")
  return(c(tau = test$estimate, p_value = test$p.value))
})

# Format results
kendall_summary <- as.data.frame(t(kendall_results))
round(kendall_summary, 3)

# Plot results for visual inspection (Appendix S12) 
tiff(file = here("figs/cook_raw_t.tiff"), width = 180, height = 100, units = "mm", res = 300)
par(mfrow = c(2, 4), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1)) 
sapply(seq_along(cook_cols), function(i) {
               col_name <- cook_cols[i]
               name <- names[i]
  plot(y=cwm_values[[col_name]], x=log10(cwm_values$samp_size),
       cex.main = 0.8,
       ylab = "Cook's Distance",
       xlab = "Sample effort (log10)",
       main = paste0(name, " (Raw)"),
       pch = 19, col = rgb(0, 0, 0, 0.5),
       ylim = c(0,2)
  ) 
  
  # Add line in plots marking one Cook`s distance unit
  abline(h = 1, col = "red", lty = 2)
})
dev.off()

```
